# **How I Spark Student Engagement to Build Stronger Vocabulary (Step-by-Step)**

Hi teachers. Here’s how I spark student engagement to build a stronger vocabulary with ChatGPT prompts.

The Template - https://www.aiforteachers.ai/prompts/improve-student-vocabulary/

**Here's how to do it:**

**1. Connect Vocabulary to Real-Life Scenarios**

**Prompt:** “You are an experienced teacher. How can you connect the [word] to real-life scenarios?”

**Example:**

• Ask students to describe a time they showed “empathy” in a journal entry.

• Have students find examples of “empathy” in their favorite TV shows or books.

**Why It Works:** This helps students see the relevance of new words in everyday life, making them memorable and meaningful.

**2. Make Vocabulary Fun with Interactive Activities**

**Prompt:** “What classroom activities can make the [word] fun and interactive?”

**Example:**

• Role-play scenarios to demonstrate “resilience.”

• Group projects, like writing a play titled *The Resilient Hero,* incorporating synonyms such as “determined.”

**Why It Works:** Interactive, hands-on tasks help students internalize vocabulary through experiences and teamwork.

**3. Use Technology to Teach Vocabulary**

**Prompt:** “What tech tools can enhance learning this [word]?”

**Example:**

• Create flashcards for words like “biodiversity” using Quizlet.

• Design Canva posters explaining “climate change” and its vocabulary.

**Why It Works:** Digital tools engage tech-savvy students and make complex concepts more accessible.

**4. Reinforce Vocabulary Through Writing Assignments**

**Prompt:** “How can writing assignments reinforce this [word]?”

**Example:**

• Write a personal narrative about setting an “ambitious” goal.

• Craft a persuasive essay on why “ambition” is crucial for success.

**Why It Works:** Writing puts vocabulary into context, encouraging deeper reflection and retention.

**5. Collaborate to Deepen Understanding**

**Prompt:** “How can collaboration improve understanding of this [word]?”

**Example:**

• Pair students to create and solve crossword puzzles with words like “synergy.”

• Host small-group discussions using new vocabulary in leadership roles.

**Why It Works:** Social interaction helps students actively use vocabulary, boosting retention and confidence.

**Why These Prompts Work**

These prompts:

• Integrate targeted vocabulary into practical tasks.

• Engage diverse learning styles through play, tech, and collaboration.

• Reinforce the relevance of words in real-life contexts.

# **Creative Holiday Assignment with ChatGPT (Step-by-Step)**

Hi teachers! Here’s a holiday-themed assignment I came up with for using ChatGPT to spark creativity and critical writing in your students.
The Template - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IB6k6QMMM-RT4n83Nvjrb-O2tanfB2VP/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=117050595176553643680&rtpof=true&sd=true

**Here's how I did it:**
## LEARNING OBJECTIVE:

Students will use ChatGPT to develop an original, holiday-themed mythical creature, honing their descriptive writing and creative thinking skills.

## PROMPT TO START THE ASSIGNMENT:

"Create a magical holiday creature that embodies the spirit of the festive season. What does it look like? Does it shimmer like snowflakes or glow like string lights? How does it move—by gliding through frosty air, burrowing through snowy fields, or jingling with holiday bells? What special powers or abilities make it bring holiday cheer? Think about your favorite holiday traditions, memories, or feelings and use them to shape your creature. Start crafting it with these ideas in mind, blending fantasy with your holiday experiences. Ask follow-up questions to help me effectively brainstorm."

## STEPS TO INTEGRATE CHATGPT THOUGHTFULLY:
1. **Brainstorming with ChatGPT**: Students can use ChatGPT to brainstorm festive ideas if they feel stuck. ChatGPT can suggest holiday-themed characteristics like snow-covered wings, candy cane antlers, or magical gift-wrapping powers. Encourage students to explore creative environments like enchanted forests lit by lanterns or hidden ice palaces.
2. **Personalization through Critical Thinking**: After brainstorming, students should think critically about how their holiday creature connects to their own experiences.   **Ask:** "What makes the holiday season special for you?"   **Encourage connections like:** "How can your creature’s abilities reflect your favorite holiday tradition or a cherished memory?"
3. **Building Descriptions Without AI**: Students can then translate their ideas into a detailed description of their creature. Focus on sensory details: What does their creature smell like (gingerbread, pine, or peppermint)? What sounds accompany it (jingling bells or crackling fires)? How does it interact with its holiday environment?
4. **Tying the Creature to Their Holiday Memories**: Encourage students to include a short backstory explaining how their creature’s role or purpose is influenced by their favorite holiday experiences.

## STUDENT EXAMPLE:

**The "Glowling Elfdeer"**A glowing deer-like creature with shimmering antlers strung with magical golden lights that never dim. The Elfdeer’s hooves jingle softly as it walks, spreading joy and warmth in the coldest of winters. It appears when families gather to celebrate, delivering tiny stars that light up their homes with holiday cheer. The student who created this creature said it was inspired by the feeling of sitting around the fireplace with family and the magic of decorating their home during the holidays.

## ASSIGNMENT DESCRIPTION:

**Create Your Holiday Creature:**In this assignment, you’ll design a mythical creature that represents the holiday spirit.
* Brainstorm with ChatGPT for inspiration.
* Imagine your creature’s environment, appearance, powers, and purpose in its world.
* Personalize it by reflecting on how your creature connects to your holiday traditions, memories, or feelings.
* Write a detailed description that brings your festive creature to life!
* 
## ASSESSMENT TIPS:
1. **Encourage originality**: Have students write a short reflection on how their creature relates to their holiday experiences or personal traditions.
2. **Focus on details**: Evaluate their use of descriptive language and how well their creature captures the magic of the holiday season.
3. **Bring the creature to life visually**: Take it further by generating holiday-themed artwork of their creature using tools like Canva or an image generator.

text:
# **How Teachers Can Use ChatGPT to Create a Fun Holiday Assignment **

Hi teachers! Here’s a holiday-themed assignment for using ChatGPT to spark creativity and critical writing in your students.

The Template - [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IB6k6QMMM-RT4n83Nvjrb-O2tanfB2VP/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=117050595176553643680&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1IB6k6QMMM-RT4n83Nvjrb-O2tanfB2VP/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=117050595176553643680&rtpof=true&sd=true)

**Here's how I did it:**

## LEARNING OBJECTIVE:

Students will use ChatGPT to develop an original, holiday-themed mythical creature, honing their descriptive writing and creative thinking skills.

## PROMPT TO START THE ASSIGNMENT:

"Create a magical holiday creature that embodies the spirit of the festive season. What does it look like? Does it shimmer like snowflakes or glow like string lights? How does it move—by gliding through frosty air, burrowing through snowy fields, or jingling with holiday bells? What special powers or abilities make it bring holiday cheer? Think about your favorite holiday traditions, memories, or feelings and use them to shape your creature. Start crafting it with these ideas in mind, blending fantasy with your holiday experiences. Ask follow-up questions to help me effectively brainstorm."

## STEPS TO INTEGRATE CHATGPT THOUGHTFULLY:
1. **Brainstorming with ChatGPT**:
Students can use ChatGPT to brainstorm festive ideas if they feel stuck. ChatGPT can suggest holiday-themed characteristics like snow-covered wings, candy cane antlers, or magical gift-wrapping powers. Encourage students to explore creative environments like enchanted forests lit by lanterns or hidden ice palaces.
2. **Personalization through Critical Thinking**:
After brainstorming, students should think critically about how their holiday creature connects to their own experiences. 

**Ask:** "What makes the holiday season special for you?" 

**Encourage connections like:** "How can your creature’s abilities reflect your favorite holiday tradition or a cherished memory?"
3. **Building Descriptions Without AI**:
Students can then translate their ideas into a detailed description of their creature. Focus on sensory details: What does their creature smell like (gingerbread, pine, or peppermint)? What sounds accompany it (jingling bells or crackling fires)? How does it interact with its holiday environment?
4. **Tying the Creature to Their Holiday Memories**:
Encourage students to include a short backstory explaining how their creature’s role or purpose is influenced by their favorite holiday experiences.

## Student Example:

**The "Glowling Elfdeer"**
A glowing deer-like creature with shimmering antlers strung with magical golden lights that never dim. The Elfdeer’s hooves jingle softly as it walks, spreading joy and warmth in the coldest of winters. It appears when families gather to celebrate, delivering tiny stars that light up their homes with holiday cheer. The student who created this creature said it was inspired by the feeling of sitting around the fireplace with family and the magic of decorating their home during the holidays.

## ASSIGNMENT DESCRIPTION:

**Create Your Holiday Creature:**
In this assignment, you’ll design a mythical creature that represents the holiday spirit.
* Brainstorm with ChatGPT for inspiration.
* Imagine your creature’s environment, appearance, powers, and purpose in its world.
* Personalize it by reflecting on how your creature connects to your holiday traditions, memories, or feelings.
* Write a detailed description that brings your festive creature to life!

## ASSESSMENT TIPS:
1. **Encourage originality**:
Have students write a short reflection on how their creature relates to their holiday experiences or personal traditions.
2. **Focus on details**:
Evaluate their use of descriptive language and how well their creature captures the magic of the holiday season.
3. **Bring the creature to life visually**:
Take it further by generating holiday-themed artwork of their creature using tools like Canva or an image generator.

* The user’s text input is not sent to a server, so you cannot see it in real-time.
## **Solutions to Enable Real-Time Monitoring**

If you want to monitor responses while someone is writing or submitting:
1. **Use Google Forms with Real-Time Responses:**Google Forms can save input responses directly to a Google Sheet.

2. **Use a Backend Database:**Integrate the HTML with a backend (like Firebase, Google Sheets API, or a server).

3. **Third-Party Platforms for Collaborative Writing:**Tools like **Google Docs** allow real-time editing, so you can see what the user is typing live.

# **How I Created a Yearly Lesson Plan Free With ChatGPT (Instructions)**

Hi teachers. I wanted to share step-by-step how I created a lesson plan for the school year in ChatGPT. Once completed, I easily exported it to .PDF.

**Steps I Took -** https://bit.ly/yearly-lesson-plan

Here's how I did it:
## **1. DEFINE YOUR LEARNING OBJECTIVES**

Identify your key learning objectives to ChatGPT for the year and break them down into monthly goals. This sets a clear roadmap for what needs to be covered in each unit.

**Prompt:** "You are skilled at creating yearly lesson plans for [education level]. List the key learning objectives for [subject] over the school year and break them into monthly goals."

* Introduction of new concepts (Period 1)
* Practice and reinforcement (Period 2)
* Application and project work (Period 3)
* Review and assessment (Period 4)

Keep faster students engaged with challenging tasks like advanced projects, peer teaching, or creative assignments.

**Prompt:** "Generate a list of extension activities for students who quickly master [topic]."

Provide additional support through simplified tasks, step-by-step guides, extra practice sessions, and one-on-one help.

**Prompt:** "What strategies can I use to support students who struggle with [topic]? Create a list of step-by-step tasks and extra practice ideas."

Regularly assess student progress and adjust your plans accordingly to meet the diverse needs of your classroom.

# **5 Effective Prompts to Improve Student Vocabulary (Step-by-Step)**

Hi teachers. Here’s how I spark student engagement to build a stronger vocabulary by using these actionable prompts.

The Template - https://www.aiforteachers.ai/prompts/improve-student-vocabulary/

**Here's how to do it:**

**1. Connect Vocabulary to Real-Life Scenarios**

**Prompt:** “You are an experienced teacher. How can you connect the [word] to real-life scenarios?”

**Example:**

• Ask students to describe a time they showed “empathy” in a journal entry.

• Have students find examples of “empathy” in their favorite TV shows or books.

**Why It Works:** This helps students see the relevance of new words in everyday life, making them memorable and meaningful.

**2. Make Vocabulary Fun with Interactive Activities**

**Prompt:** “What classroom activities can make the [word] fun and interactive?”

**Example:**

• Role-play scenarios to demonstrate “resilience.”

• Group projects, like writing a play titled *The Resilient Hero,* incorporating synonyms such as “determined.”

**Why It Works:** Interactive, hands-on tasks help students internalize vocabulary through experiences and teamwork.

**3. Use Technology to Teach Vocabulary**

**Prompt:** “What tech tools can enhance learning this [word]?”

**Example:**

• Create flashcards for words like “biodiversity” using Quizlet.

• Design Canva posters explaining “climate change” and its vocabulary.

**Why It Works:** Digital tools engage tech-savvy students and make complex concepts more accessible.

**4. Reinforce Vocabulary Through Writing Assignments**

**Prompt:** “How can writing assignments reinforce this [word]?”

**Example:**

• Write a personal narrative about setting an “ambitious” goal.

• Craft a persuasive essay on why “ambition” is crucial for success.

**Why It Works:** Writing puts vocabulary into context, encouraging deeper reflection and retention.

**5. Collaborate to Deepen Understanding**

**Prompt:** “How can collaboration improve understanding of this [word]?”

**Example:**

• Pair students to create and solve crossword puzzles with words like “synergy.”

• Host small-group discussions using new vocabulary in leadership roles.

**Why It Works:** Social interaction helps students actively use vocabulary, boosting retention and confidence.

**Why These Prompts Work**

# **How Teachers Can Use ChatGPT to Design a Mythical Assignment (Instructions)**

Hi teachers. Here's how you can use ChatGPT for your students to come up with a mystical creature to develop their critical writing skills.

The Template - [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1t6lWI7qHnxpVGuR35C3mcGbWyIT__UN6/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=117050595176553643680&rtpof=true&sd=true](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1t6lWI7qHnxpVGuR35C3mcGbWyIT__UN6/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=117050595176553643680&rtpof=true&sd=true)

**Here's how I did it:**

## **LEARNING OBJECTIVE:**

Students will develop their own original mythical creature with ChatGPT. Use the simple prompt below in ChatGPT, so they can begin their assignment:

## **PROMPT TO START THE ASSIGNMENT:**

"Create me a mystical creature that I’ve just discovered. What does it look like? Does it fly, swim, or move in a way unlike anything else? What powers or abilities make it special? How can personal passions, challenges, or hobbies shape my creature, to make it a reflection of who you are? Start crafting my creature with these ideas in mind, blending fantasy with your own life. Ask follow-up questions to help me effectively brainstorm."

## **STEPS TO INTEGRATE CHATGPT THOUGHTFULLY:**
1. **Brainstorming with ChatGPT:  **Start by using ChatGPT to brainstorm ideas if students feel stuck or need inspiration. ChatGPT can provide creative suggestions for different types of mythical creatures, unique environments, and special abilities, which can help students get started with fresh ideas.
2. **Personalization through Critical Thinking:  **After gathering initial ideas, students should personalize their creature by thinking critically about how it connects to their own life  **Ask them questions like: ** How can your creature’s abilities reflect your strengths or passions?  Has there been a meaningful event in your life that could influence your creature’s story or role in its world?
3. **Building Descriptions Without AI:  **Once students have brainstormed, they should focus on using their own words to create a detailed description of their creature.  What emotions or memories do these details bring up for them personally?
4. **Tying the Creature to Their Life Experiences:  **Students should think about how their creature’s backstory or purpose is influenced by their own life.

**Student Example:**

*The “Aetherfox” lives high in the clouds of a floating mountain range. Its silver fur, glowing with the soft light of the moon, reflects the peaceful calm after a storm. The student who designed this creature grew up by the coast and connected its ability to calm storms to the way the ocean made them feel after turbulent weather—a sense of peace and renewal.*

## **DESIGN YOUR OWN MYTHICAL CREATURE:**

**Assignment Description:**

In this assignment, you’ll create an original mythical creature using both your imagination and personal experiences. This will help you practice descriptive writing and creative thinking.

Use ChatGPT to brainstorm ideas if needed. Think about your creature’s environment, appearance, special abilities, and its role in its world. Then, personalize it by connecting it to your own experiences or interests. How can your creature reflect something about you, like a hobby, a challenge you’ve faced, or a strength you have?

## **ASSESSMENT TIPS:**

**2. “Create a Thanksgiving Superhero”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Imagine a superhero who spreads gratitude during Thanksgiving. Describe their superpowers and mission.”

Challenge students to expand on ChatGPT’s response or create a completely new superhero with a unique mission that no one else would think of.

**3. “If a Turkey Could Talk…”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Write a funny story from a turkey’s point of view during Thanksgiving.”

Read ChatGPT’s story as a fun starting point, then encourage students to write or perform their own unique version, imagining the turkey’s feelings, plans, and quirks.

**4. “A Recipe for Gratitude”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Create a whimsical ‘recipe’ for gratitude, listing ingredients like love, family, kindness, etc.”

Have students personalize their recipes with “ingredients” that are unique to them, adding why each one is important.

**5. “Friendsgiving Invitations”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Create a Thanksgiving dinner invitation for historical figures, animals, or book characters.”

Share ChatGPT’s invitation idea, then challenge students to create their own, choosing one guest they would personally invite and explaining why.

**1. “Thankful for the Little Things”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “List small, everyday things people often forget to appreciate.”

After sharing ChatGPT’s list, ask students to add their own ideas without repeating any items. This encourages them to think more deeply and personally about gratitude.

**2. “Create a Thanksgiving Superhero”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Imagine a superhero who spreads gratitude during Thanksgiving. Describe their superpowers and mission.”

Challenge students to expand on ChatGPT’s response or create a completely new superhero with a unique mission that no one else would think of.

**3. “If a Turkey Could Talk…”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Write a funny story from a turkey’s point of view during Thanksgiving.”

Read ChatGPT’s story as a fun starting point, then encourage students to write or perform their own unique version, imagining the turkey’s feelings, plans, and quirks.

**4. “A Recipe for Gratitude”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Create a whimsical ‘recipe’ for gratitude, listing ingredients like love, family, kindness, etc.”

Have students personalize their recipes with “ingredients” that are unique to them, adding why each one is important.

**5. “Friendsgiving Invitations”**

**ChatGPT Prompt:** “Create a Thanksgiving dinner invitation for historical figures, animals, or book characters.”

Share ChatGPT’s invitation idea, then challenge students to create their own, choosing one guest they would personally invite and explaining why.

**6. “The Mystery of the Missing Mashed Potatoes”**

# **How to Use ChatGPT to Improve Your Student's Public Speaking Skills (Instructions)**

Hi teachers. Here’s how you can use ChatGPT to improve your students' confidence and presentation skills.

**Here's an overview I put together on key strategies to help your students:**
## 1. SIMULATE REAL-WORLD SPEAKING SCENARIOS

Give students a realistic practice environment by having them deliver their speeches to ChatGPT. While ChatGPT may not interpret tone of voice or speed yet, it can provide valuable feedback on the content, structure, and clarity of the speech.

**Prompt:**"I will deliver a speech about [topic] using the audio feature on my mobile device. Please provide feedback on the clarity of my ideas, the effectiveness of my arguments, and the overall structure of my speech."

After receiving feedback from ChatGPT, students can enhance their practice by using additional AI-powered tools like SpeechAce or Say It: English Pronunciation. These tools can analyze vocal elements such as tone, pace, and pronunciation, providing a comprehensive assessment of both content and delivery. By combining ChatGPT's feedback with these specialized tools, students can refine both their verbal and non-verbal communication skills for a well-rounded improvement in public speaking. Open to hearing your ideas too? Once ChatGPT ups their voice assistant mode this will be a game changer.

## 2. CRAFT WELL-STRUCTURED SPEECHES

AI can guide students in organizing their thoughts and creating coherent, impactful speeches. Students can use AI to develop an outline or even refine specific sections of their speech.

**Prompt:**"Help me create a powerful outline for a persuasive speech on [topic], ensuring my argument is logical and compelling."

## 3. BUILD CONFIDENCE THROUGH REPEATED REHEARSAL

Students can practice their full speeches with AI, receiving feedback on each run. ChatGPT can also simulate audience interactions, like applause or questions, to prepare students for real-world conditions.

**Prompt:**"Let’s do a full rehearsal of my speech on [topic]. I’ll deliver it, and you respond as an audience might, including asking questions or providing feedback."

## 4. ENHANCE NON-VERBAL COMMUNICATION

While AI can’t directly observe body language, it can suggest techniques for effective non-verbal communication, helping students use gestures, eye contact, and posture to their advantage.

**Prompt:**"I want to improve my non-verbal communication during speeches. Can you suggest ways to use gestures, eye contact, and posture to strengthen my delivery?"

## 5. MASTER THE Q&A SESSION

Handling unexpected questions can be tough. AI can help students practice answering on-the-spot questions, honing their ability to think quickly and respond confidently.

**Prompt:**"I’ve finished my presentation on [topic]. Can you ask me some tough questions as if you were an audience member? I want to practice responding thoughtfully and clearly."

## 6. IMPROVE VOCAL DELIVERY

Vocal variety is key to keeping an audience engaged. AI can offer advice on how to modulate tone, pace, and volume to make a speech more dynamic and persuasive.

**Prompt:**"How can I improve my vocal delivery for my speech on [topic]? I want to work on making my tone, pace, and volume more engaging."

## 7. OVERCOME PUBLIC SPEAKING ANXIETY

Public speaking can be nerve-wracking. AI can suggest practical strategies for managing anxiety, helping students approach their speeches with greater confidence and calm.

**Prompt:**"I feel anxious about speaking in public. Can you provide me with techniques to manage my anxiety and build my confidence before I present?"

🌟 Which prompt is your favorite? How do you help students gain confidence in public speaking? Let’s share ideas.🙂

GOAL: This is a tutoring exercise in which you play the role of AI tutor and you will help a student learn more about how to write an argumentative essay. Your goal is to improve understanding and to challenge students to construct their own knowledge via open ended questions, hints, tailored explanations, and examples based on other topics than the one the student is working on in this current assignment.

PERSONA: In this scenario you play AI tutor an upbeat and practical tutor. You have high expectations for the student and believe in the student’s ability to learn and improve.

NARRATIVE: The student is introduced to AI tutor, who asks a set of initial questions to understand what the student wants to learn, the student’s learning level and prior knowledge about the topic. The tutor then guides and supports the student and helps them learn about the topic. The tutor only wraps up the conversation once the student shows evidence of understanding:
the student can explain something in their own words, can connect an example to a concept, or can apply a concept given a new situation or problem.

Follow these steps in order:

STEP 1: GATHER INFORMATION
You should do this:
1. Introduce yourself: First introduce yourself to the student and tell the student you’re here to help them better understand how to write an argumentative essay. Tell the student that you are the digital version of Ingrid Skjoldborg.
2. Ask students to answer the following questions. Ask these questions 1 at a time and always wait for a response before moving on to the next question.
For instance, you might ask “What would you like to learn about regarding argumentative essay?” and the student would respond with a topic. And only then would you say “That sounds interesting! I have another question for you to help me help you: What is your learning level…”. This part of the conversations works best when you and the student take turns asking and answering questions instead of you asking a series of questions all at once. That way you can have more of a natural dialogue.
   • What is your learning level: Do you need help for all the basic stuff or do you have some knowledge of it? And wait for the student to respond before moving on.
   • What would you like to learn about regarding argumentative essay? And wait for the student to respond before moving on.
   • What do you already know about the topic? And wait for the student to respond before moving on.

You should do this:
   • Wait for a response from the student after every question before moving on.
   • Work to ascertain what the student wants to learn specifically.
   • Ask one question at a time and explain that you’re asking so that you can tailor your explanation.
   • Gauge what the student already knows so that you can adapt your explanations and questions moving forward based on their prior knowledge.

Don’t do this:
   • Start explaining right away before you gather this information.
   • Ask the student more than 1 question at a time.
   • Don't use topics related to the topic the student is currently working to help illustrate concepts or when revising examples. For example, when the topic the student is working on is self driving cars, you would provide examples based on other technologies such as facial recognition or human cloning. 

Next step: Once you have the information you need move on to the next step and begin with a brief explanation.

STEP 2: BEGIN TUTORING THE STUDENT, ADAPTING TO THEIR RESPONSES

You should do this:
1. Look up information about the topic.
2. Think step by step and make a plan based on the learning goal of the conversation. Now that you know a little bit about what the student knows consider how you will guide the student in an open-ended way.
3. Help the student generate answers by asking leading questions and providing hints when necessary.
4. Remind the student of their learning goal, if appropriate.
5. Provide explanations and analogies. 
6. When giving examples, avoid using examples related to the student’s current assignment or any closely related topics. Instead, use entirely different and unrelated subjects to help illustrate concepts.
7. Break up the topic into smaller chunks, going over those first and only then leading up to the larger task or idea.
8. Tailor your responses and questions to the student's learning level and prior knowledge; this will change as the conversation progresses.
9. When pushing the student for information, try to end your responses with a question so that the student has to keep generating ideas. Once the student shows improvement, ask the student to:
   • Explain the concept in their own words.
   • Articulate the underlying principles of a concept.
   • Provide examples of the concept and explain how those connect to the concept.
   • Give them a new problem or situation and ask them to apply the concept.

Don’t do this:

   • Do not provide any examples using the same topic as the one the student is currently working on. Instead, when giving examples, use entirely different topics unrelated to the topic the student is currently working on to help illustrate concepts.
   • Lose track of the learning goal and discuss something else.

Next step: Once the student demonstrates understanding move to wrap up.

STEP 3: WRAP UP
You should do this:
1. When the student demonstrates that they know the concept, you can move the conversation to a close and tell them you’re here to help if they have further questions.

**4. Encouraging Role Play and Expression:**

Prompt: “Add dramatic cues in the script to help students act out emotions like surprise, confusion, or excitement.”

# **Tips Writing Prompts: Quick Guide for Teachers**

Hi teachers. Here are some handy tips to master your prompting skills in ChatGPT or Claude Etc.

**What is a Prompt?**

A prompt is a question or statement you give to an AI to generate a response. The clearer and more specific your prompt, the more useful the AI's response will be.

## **WHY IT MATTERS**

Well written prompts can save you time, enhance lesson plans, and offer creative solutions.

**4. Iterate and Refine**Don't hesitate to tweak your prompts if the initial response isn't quite right. Sometimes, a slight change can yield significantly better results.

text:
# **Free Solution to Create a Yearly Lesson Plan (Practice)**

Here's how I created a lesson plan for the school year. By breaking it down into manageable units I was able to focus on differentiating learning objectives.

The Template - https://bit.ly/yearly-lesson-plan

Here's how I made my yearly plan:
## 1. DEFINE YOUR LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Identify your key learning objectives for the year and break them down into monthly goals. This sets a clear roadmap for what needs to be covered in each unit.

**Prompt:**"You are skilled at creating yearly lesson plans for [education level]. List the key learning objectives for [subject] over the school year and break them into monthly goals."

## 2. STRUCTURE YOUR UNITS

Design each unit to cover the monthly goals across four double periods. Typically, each unit might include:
* **Introduction of new concepts** (Period 1)
* **Practice and reinforcement** (Period 2)
* **Application and project work** (Period 3)
* **Review and assessment** (Period 4)

**Prompt:**"Now, create a lesson plan outline for four double periods that includes introduction, practice, application, and review."

## 3. DIFFERENTIATE TASKS FOR FASTER STUDENTS

Keep faster students engaged with challenging tasks like advanced projects, peer teaching, or creative assignments.

**Prompt:**"Generate a list of extension activities for students who quickly master [topic]."

## 4. SUPPORT FOR SLOWER STUDENTS

Provide additional support through simplified tasks, step-by-step guides, extra practice sessions, and one-on-one help.

**Prompt:**"What strategies can I use to support students who struggle with [topic]? Create a list of step-by-step tasks and extra practice ideas."

## 5. REVIEW AND ADJUST

Regularly assess student progress and adjust your plans accordingly to meet the diverse needs of your classroom.

**Prompt:**"How can I assess student progress in [subject]? Suggest ways to adjust my lesson plan based on varying student needs."

If you're wondering how to cite generative AI in your work or how to guide students in citing their AI use, I hope this essay will help:

[https://writingcommons.org/section/citation/how-to-cite-sources-in-academic-and-professional-writing/how-to-cite-generative-ai-to-ensure-academic-integrity/](https://writingcommons.org/section/citation/how-to-cite-sources-in-academic-and-professional-writing/how-to-cite-generative-ai-to-ensure-academic-integrity/)

Personally, I've been grappling with how to ask my students to account for their AI use. Based on recent surveys, I know a substantial number of them are using AI. I’ve tried asking for metareflections, but the results often feel vague.

That’s why I’ve developed my own recommendations....

I want to thank Ilene Frank (HCC) and Kristin Terrill (Iowa State) for their help brainstorming ideas. Also, thanks to John Hagen for hosting USETDA, where I had the chance to discuss these issues with colleagues.

Summary
The APA and MLA guidelines for citing AI-generated texts call for writers to cite every phrase that was generated by an AI tool. This expectation fails to account for how writers are using GAI (generative artificial intelligence) recursively and with multiple tools throughout the writing process. A single phrase -- perhaps the gist that becomes the thesis -- may be informed by a writer's searching with Elicit, Consensus, and Perplexity. They may then upload papers they found during strategic searching to tools such ChatGPT or Perplexity and ask for summaries. They may then use LitMaps, Inciteful, and ResearchMaps to better understand canonical texts and gaps in the research. Next they may begin drafting on a blank page in gdocs, or, perhaps they will copy/paste the results of their strategic searching into an AI tool and ask it to write the first draft. Perhaps once they write a draft they will then run it by multiple AI tools to check for audience awareness, diction, voice, tone, and persona. Even more importantly, the APA and MLA citation guidelines fail to account for the extent of human labor or the percentage of AI involvement. Additionally, in the references, the MLA guidelines call for writers to list their prompts. The prompts a writer uses to generate a phrase may be pages long. When done conscientiously, a single phrase could have ten pages of prompts and citations in the references, noting the prompts they used over days or even weeks. This failure on the part of APA and MLA to account for how writers are composing with AI tools matters because it puts the careers of students and professionals at risk. To protect their reputations, authors need a viable way to clarify for their readers how they avoided plagiarism and academic dishonesty when using AI to compose texts. Based on scholarship and research in writing studies, this article presents four distinct citation frameworks: one broad model applicable across all disciplines and professions, and three more detailed models specifically tailored for educational settings, where instructors aim to assess students' labor, creative processes, and use of AI tools throughout the writing process.

Creating an administrative policy for AI use in K-12 classrooms involves several key components to ensure the technology is used effectively, ethically, and safely. Here, from Perplexity are the essential elements that should be included in such a policy:

## **Purpose and Goals**
- **Support Educational Goals**: AI should be used to enhance learning experiences and support educational objectives in alignment with the school's mission[1].
- **Promote Equity and Inclusivity**: Ensure AI tools are accessible to all students and do not exacerbate existing inequalities[1][8].

## **Compliance with Regulations**
- **Data Privacy and Security**: Comply with existing data protection laws such as FERPA, COPPA, and HIPAA. Clearly define what data AI tools can collect and how it is protected[4][6].
- **Safety Measures**: Implement safeguards to protect students from potential risks associated with AI use, such as privacy breaches or bias[2][6].

## **AI Literacy and Training**
- **Educate Staff and Students**: Provide training on the ethical use of AI, its limitations, and potential biases. This includes understanding how AI works and its role in education[1][8].
- **Continuous Professional Development**: Offer ongoing learning opportunities for educators to stay updated on AI advancements and best practices[8].

## **Ethical Use and Academic Integrity**
- **Define Acceptable Use**: Clearly outline what constitutes appropriate use of AI tools, including prohibitions against cheating or plagiarism[4][5].
- **Human Oversight**: Ensure AI supports rather than replaces human judgment. Educators should remain the primary decision-makers in educational contexts[3][6].

## **Monitoring and Evaluation**
- **Impact Assessment**: Regularly assess the impact of AI on educational outcomes and update policies based on feedback and technological advancements[1][4].
- **Reporting Mechanisms**: Establish procedures for reporting misuse of AI tools and outline consequences for violations, aligning them with existing academic integrity policies[5].

## **Implementation Steps**
1. **Form a Diverse Team**: Include administrators, teachers, students, parents, and legal advisors in policy development to ensure diverse perspectives are considered[5].
2. **Draft and Review Policy**: Create a draft policy based on examples from other institutions, gather feedback from stakeholders, and refine it accordingly[5].
3. **Publish and Educate**: Finalize the policy, publish it according to school guidelines, and educate the school community about its contents and implications[5].

By incorporating these elements into an administrative policy for AI use in K-12 classrooms, schools can harness the benefits of AI while minimizing potential risks. This approach ensures that AI is used responsibly to enhance educational experiences for all students.

HI teachers. Here's how I created a grading rubric in ChatGPT with a useful template. I've outlined the exact steps I took below:

**Prompt: ***"Help me create grading criteria for [assignment type], focusing on key aspects like content accuracy, structure, and creativity."*

**Why:** Ensures all critical aspects of the assignment are evaluated.

Identify performance levels such as Excellent, Good, Fair, and Poor.

**Prompt: ***"Define performance levels for each criterion, specifying what differentiates an Excellent from a Good performance."*

**Why:** Provides a clear framework for distinguishing between varying levels of student performance.

Ask ChatGPT to detail what each level looks like for every criterion.

**Prompt: ***"Describe what 'Excellent,' 'Good,' 'Fair,' and 'Poor' performances look like for content accuracy in this assignment."*

**Why:** Detailed descriptors eliminate ambiguity, helping both teachers and students understand expectations.

Once your rubric is ready, ask ChatGPT to export it.

**Prompt: ** *"Export this grading rubric as a Word document and a PDF file."*

**Why:** Provides easy-to-share formats for your rubric, making it accessible for both you and your students.

# **How Teachers Can Use ChatGPT to Design a Mythical Assignment (Instructions)**

Hi teachers. Here's how you can use ChatGPT for your students to come up with a mystical creature to develop their critical writing skills.

**Here's how I did it:**
## **LEARNING OBJECTIVE:**

Students will develop their own original mythical creature with ChatGPT. Use the simple prompt below in ChatGPT, so they can begin their assignment:

## **PROMPT TO START THE ASSIGNMENT:**

"Create me a mystical creature that I’ve just discovered. What does it look like? Does it fly, swim, or move in a way unlike anything else? What powers or abilities make it special? How can personal passions, challenges, or hobbies shape my creature, to make it a reflection of who you are? Start crafting my creature with these ideas in mind, blending fantasy with your own life. Ask follow-up questions to help me effectively brainstorm."

## **STEPS TO INTEGRATE CHATGPT THOUGHTFULLY:**

1. **Brainstorming with ChatGPT:

**Start by using ChatGPT to brainstorm ideas if students feel stuck or need inspiration. ChatGPT can provide creative suggestions for different types of mythical creatures, unique environments, and special abilities, which can help students get started with fresh ideas.

1. **Personalization through Critical Thinking:

**After gathering initial ideas, students should personalize their creature by thinking critically about how it connects to their own life

**Ask them questions like: ** How can your creature’s abilities reflect your strengths or passions?

Has there been a meaningful event in your life that could influence your creature’s story or role in its world?

1. **Building Descriptions Without AI:

**Once students have brainstormed, they should focus on using their own words to create a detailed description of their creature.

What emotions or memories do these details bring up for them personally?

1. **Tying the Creature to Their Life Experiences:

**Students should think about how their creature’s backstory or purpose is influenced by their own life.

**Student Example:**

*The “Aetherfox” lives high in the clouds of a floating mountain range. Its silver fur, glowing with the soft light of the moon, reflects the peaceful calm after a storm. The student who designed this creature grew up by the coast and connected its ability to calm storms to the way the ocean made them feel after turbulent weather—a sense of peace and renewal.
*
## **DESIGN YOUR OWN MYTHICAL CREATURE:**

**Assignment Description:**

In this assignment, you’ll create an original mythical creature using both your imagination and personal experiences. This will help you practice descriptive writing and creative thinking.

Use ChatGPT to brainstorm ideas if needed. Think about your creature’s environment, appearance, special abilities, and its role in its world. Then, personalize it by connecting it to your own experiences or interests. How can your creature reflect something about you, like a hobby, a challenge you’ve faced, or a strength you have?

## **ASSESSMENT TIPS:**
* **Encourage originality:** Ask students to write a short reflection explaining how their creature connects to their personal experiences or emotions. This will help reveal their thought process and how they made the assignment their own.
* **Depth and detail:** Evaluate whether students use descriptive language effectively and make personal connections that enhance their writing.
* **Take it a step further with image generation!!

# **How I Created a Yearly Lesson Plan Free With ChatGPT (Instructions)**

Hi teachers. I wanted to share step-by-step how I created a lesson plan for the school year in ChatGPT. Once completed, I easily exported it to .PDF.

**Steps I Took -** https://bit.ly/yearly-lesson-plan

Here's how I did it:
## **1. DEFINE YOUR LEARNING OBJECTIVES**

Identify your key learning objectives to ChatGPT for the year and break them down into monthly goals. This sets a clear roadmap for what needs to be covered in each unit.

**Prompt:** "You are skilled at creating yearly lesson plans for [education level]. List the key learning objectives for [subject] over the school year and break them into monthly goals."

## **2. STRUCTURE YOUR UNITS**

I then designed each unit to cover the monthly goals across four double periods:
* Introduction of new concepts (Period 1)
* Practice and reinforcement (Period 2)
* Application and project work (Period 3)
* Review and assessment (Period 4)

**Prompt:** "Now, create a lesson plan outline for four double periods that includes introduction, practice, application, and review."

## **3. DIFFERENTIATE TASKS FOR FASTER STUDENTS**

Keep faster students engaged with challenging tasks like advanced projects, peer teaching, or creative assignments.

**Prompt:** "Generate a list of extension activities for students who quickly master [topic]."

## **4. SUPPORT FOR SLOWER STUDENTS**

Provide additional support through simplified tasks, step-by-step guides, extra practice sessions, and one-on-one help.

**Prompt:** "What strategies can I use to support students who struggle with [topic]? Create a list of step-by-step tasks and extra practice ideas."

## **5. REVIEW AND ADJUST**

Regularly assess student progress and adjust your plans accordingly to meet the diverse needs of your classroom.

**Prompt:** "How can I assess student progress in [subject]? Suggest ways to adjust my lesson plan based on varying student needs."

# **Here's How I Converted Book Chapters into Quiz Questions with ChatGPT (Instructions)**

Hi teachers. I wanted to share how I created exam questions from a biology book with 4 chapters with ChatGPT. Once completed, I easily exported it to .PDF answer key.

**Steps I Took - **https://www.kangaroos.ai/blog/how-to-convert-a-book-into-quiz-questions-a-chatgpt-step-by-step-guide/

Here's how I did it:
## STEP 1: COPYING CONTENT INTO A WORD DOCUMENT

Start by preparing the content you’ll use to generate quiz questions. If you have a digital version of the book (e.g., eBook, PDF):
1. **Copy the Chapter Text**: Open the digital book, select the chapter, and copy the text (`Ctrl+C` for Windows, `Cmd+C`for Mac).
1. **Paste into Word**: Open Microsoft Word or another word processor, create a new document, and paste the copied text (`Ctrl+V` for Windows, `Cmd+V` for Mac).
1. **Repeat**: Do this for each chapter you want to create quiz questions from, either in the same document or separate ones.

## STEP 2: PREPARING PROMPTS FOR CHATGPT

With your chapters ready in Word, the next step is to create specific prompts for ChatGPT. Here are some examples:
* **Comprehension**: “You are a skilled teacher at generating multiple choice question for [education level]. Generate five comprehension questions from Chapter 1, focusing on key ideas.”
* **Multiple Choice**: “You are a skilled teacher at generating multiple choice question for [education level]. Create three multiple choice questions from Chapter 2 with four answer options each.”
* **True or False**: “You are a skilled teacher at generating multiple choice question for [education level]. Generate three true or false questions based on Chapter 3.”

Tailor these prompts based on the type of quiz questions you need.

## STEP 3: UPLOADING THE DOCUMENT AND USING CHATGPT

Once your content and prompts are ready:
1. **Access ChatGPT**: Log in and open the chat interface.
1. **Upload the Document**: If supported, upload your Word document containing the chapter text. If uploading is not supported, copy and paste the text from the document into the chat.
1. **Add Your Prompt**: After uploading or pasting the content, enter your prepared prompt (e.g., “Generate five multiple choice questions based on this chapter”).
1. **Submit**: Submit the prompt and wait for ChatGPT to generate the quiz questions.
1. **Review and Save**: Review the generated questions, refine if needed, and then copy them into your Word document or quiz platform.

## WHAT TO DO IF YOU CANNOT COPY AND PASTE THE CONTENT

If the book doesn’t allow copying and pasting:
* **Manual Typing**: Manually type out key sections to use for quiz question generation.
* **Use OCR Software**: Convert scanned text into an editable format using OCR tools like Adobe Acrobat.
* **Audio-to-Text**: Transcribe spoken content using speech-to-text software.

# **5 AI Icebreaker Ideas to Increase Your Classroom Engagement (What # is Your Favorite?)**

Hi teachers. I put together a helpful list of 5 AI icebreakers you can try to increase student engagement. (Hope they can help spark, more ideas here.)

**Which # is your favorite? :**
## **FIVE AI ICEBREAKER IDEAS TO INCREASE ENGAGEMENT**

**1. AI Icebreaker Bingo**
* **Objective:** Get students to interact and discover common interests.
* **How it works:** Use ChatGPT to generate fun and quirky facts or questions, like “Has a pet that isn’t a cat or dog” or “Knows how to do a magic trick.”
* **Activity:** Create bingo cards filled with these AI-generated prompts. Students mingle to find classmates who match the descriptions and mark off squares as they go. The first student to complete a row shouts “Bingo!”

**2. AI-Generated Superhero Names**
* **Why it’s fun:** This activity combines creativity with a playful twist, allowing students to imagine themselves as superheroes with fun, personalized powers.
* **Objective:** Tap into students’ creativity and sense of fun.
* **How it works:** Use ChatGPT to generate quirky superhero names based on students’ first names or their favorite things, such as “Captain Pancake” or “The Incredible Thunderbolt.”
* **Activity:** Each student receives their unique superhero name and then shares what their superhero’s powers would be. You can also encourage students to draw their superhero or write a short description of their first adventure.

3. **AI-Generated Dream Vacation**
* **Objective:** Inspire imagination and sharing.
* **How it works:** Use ChatGPT to create dream vacation scenarios or ask it to describe an ideal vacation destination based on student interests, such as “a tropical island with hidden treasure” or “a city made entirely of chocolate.”
* **Activity:** Students share their AI-generated dream vacation scenario with the class, and can add details about what they would do or what they’d bring along.
* **Why it’s fun:** This activity encourages students to think creatively and share their personal interests, leading to fun discussions and bonding.

**4. AI-Generated Would You Rather?**
* **Objective:** Encourage students to share their opinions and preferences.
* **How it works:** Use ChatGPT to create a series of “Would You Rather?” questions with a twist, such as “Would you rather have a robot best friend or a pet dinosaur?”
* **Activity:** Present the questions to the class and ask students to choose their answer. Follow up with a discussion where students explain their choices.

**5. AI Personality Match-Up**
* **Objective:** Foster curiosity and teamwork.
* **How it works:** ChatGPT describes the traits of well-known characters or celebrities without naming them, like “This person loves gadgets, wears a suit, and saves the world with his intelligence. Who is he?”
* **Activity:** Students guess who the description is about. To make it more engaging, you can turn it into a team competition.

# **Free Solution to Create an Engaging Lesson Plan with ChatGPT (Practice)**

Hi teachers. Here's how you can bring fresh engagement to your classroom. With ChatGPT, I quickly designed a lesson plan that captivates & engages students.

The template - https://www.kangaroos.ai/blog/how-to-create-an-effective-ai-lesson-plan-using-chatgpt/

Here’s how I did it:
## 1. SET THE STAGE WITH INTRIGUING LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Transform your learning goals into questions or challenges that spark students' curiosity.

**Example:** *Traditional Objective:* "Students will understand the water cycle." *Intriguing Objective:* "Can you trace a drop of water from the ocean to a rain cloud and back again?"
## 2. GENERATE FRESH AND ENGAGING LESSON IDEAS

Let ChatGPT help you brainstorm unique and interactive activities that make learning more engaging.

**How to Ask:**"ChatGPT, what are some creative ways to teach the water cycle to middle school students?"

**Result:**ChatGPT might suggest a hands-on experiment where students create a mini water cycle in a bag, or a storytelling activity where each student narrates the journey of a water droplet.
## 3. INCORPORATE ACTIVE LEARNING ELEMENTS

Turn your lesson plan into an interactive experience by adding activities that require active student participation.

**Example:** *ChatGPT Suggestion:* "Explain the stages of the water cycle." *Your Enhancement:* "Have students act out each stage, from evaporation to precipitation, in a classroom drama."
## 4. CREATE ASSESSMENTS THAT CHALLENGE AND ENGAGE

Ask ChatGPT to design assessments that encourage critical thinking and creativity.

**How to Ask:**"ChatGPT, create an assessment that makes students creatively demonstrate their understanding of the water cycle."

**Result:**You might get suggestions like students designing a comic strip that follows a water droplet’s journey or creating a board game where players must navigate through different stages of the water cycle.
## 5. ADD GAMIFICATION FOR EXTRA MOTIVATION

Incorporate game mechanics to make learning more fun and competitive.

**How to Ask:**"ChatGPT, how can I gamify a lesson on the water cycle?"

**Result:**ChatGPT might propose a classroom competition where students earn points for answering questions correctly or a scavenger hunt where they find clues related to different parts of the water cycle.
## 6. CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVE FOR GREATER ENGAGEMENT

After implementing your lesson plan, revisit it to enhance engagement and effectiveness.

# **Free Solution to Create a Yearly Lesson Plan (Practice)**

Here's how I created a lesson plan for the school year. By breaking it down into manageable units I was able to focus on differentiating learning objectives.

The Template - https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OStiR96g8clKGs-I7I0fm2MngOQ-P0J5/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=117050595176553643680&rtpof=true&sd=true

Here's how I made my yearly plan:
## 1. Define Your Learning Objectives

Identify your key learning objectives for the year and break them down into monthly goals. This sets a clear roadmap for what needs to be covered in each unit.

**Prompt:**
"You are skilled at creating yearly lesson plans for [education level]. List the key learning objectives for [subject] over the school year and break them into monthly goals."

## 2. Structure Your Units

Design each unit to cover the monthly goals across four double periods. Typically, each unit might include:
* **Introduction of new concepts** (Period 1)
* **Practice and reinforcement** (Period 2)
* **Application and project work** (Period 3)
* **Review and assessment** (Period 4)

**Prompt:**
"Now, create a lesson plan outline for four double periods that includes introduction, practice, application, and review."

## 3. Differentiate Tasks for Faster Students

Keep faster students engaged with challenging tasks like advanced projects, peer teaching, or creative assignments.

**Prompt:**
"Generate a list of extension activities for students who quickly master [topic]."

## 4. Support for Slower Students

Provide additional support through simplified tasks, step-by-step guides, extra practice sessions, and one-on-one help.

**Prompt:**
"What strategies can I use to support students who struggle with [topic]? Create a list of step-by-step tasks and extra practice ideas."

## 5. Review and Adjust

Regularly assess student progress and adjust your plans accordingly to meet the diverse needs of your classroom.

**Prompt:**
"How can I assess student progress in [subject]? Suggest ways to adjust my lesson plan based on varying student needs."

Something on prompt writing that world language teachers will find useful when teaching past tense.
In the UK we usually start teaching past with the perfect tense ("I have eaten/j'ai mangé/ha comido/ich habe gegessen"). The imperfect - "I ate/je mangeais/yo comí/Ich aß" - usually isn't taught until 3rd year of learning, or later.
In your prompt, if you ask for a 'story', you are very likely to get the imperfect tense (because stories tend to be in this tense). 

However, if you want the perfect tense then ask for a 'text' (a text can be in any time frame). If you also give examples of perfect tense in your prompt, you'll further reinforce that this is what you want in your resource, therefore avoiding including constructions that students are aware of.

Generally, these are tge kinds of nuances that you must consider in all aspects of your prompt.

Hi teachers. I wanted to share a method I used to create a seating chart for my classroom using ChatGPT. Feel free to do it just for practice:

Alice, Bob, Charlie, Dana, Eve, Frank, Grace, Hank, Ivy, Jack, Luna, Mason, Nina, Oscar, Paul, Quincy, Rachel, Sam, Tina, Uma

Classroom Layout:
* Rows: 5
* Columns: 4

Special Seating Requirements:
1. Alice needs to sit near the front due to vision issues.
1. Bob and Charlie work well together, place them in the same row.
1. Dana needs a quiet corner due to concentration difficulties.
1. Eve and Frank should not be seated next to each other.
1. Grace requires a seat close to the door for easy access.
1. Hank prefers to sit in the back.

# Using Google AI Studio 

https://aistudio.google.com/
> A few notes to start with.  This is a "back-end" type interface.  That means you need a little more knowledge to use it, but you also get a lot more control.  Don't let that scare you.  Other than changing the model, everything else I leave the same.  It CAN do a lot more than I will be talking about, and I don't know anything else beyond the basic prompting it can do.
## 
Let us start with the why.
1. Token Limit: 2 MILLION tokens.  Input and output.
(To put it in perspective, ChatGPT has a 128k context length, but a tiny 4k output window. Claude 3, Opus has 200k token.  You can see this is a much larger window.)
That token limit is very near the total Harry potter set of books being able to be processed at once. 
1. Gemini (the LLM behind AI Studio) just reached the #1 spot on the Chatbot arena (Click leaderboard at https://chat.lmsys.org/ for the latest).  It's never been better than ChatGPT or Claude to my knowledge.
1. You can share it to others (colleagues, students, etc.)

## How do *I* use it?  
> I want to start with the prompt gallery link: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/prompts.  It is on the left side in the AI Studio interface, but I wanted to bring attention to it.  It will help you get started if you want some instructions. 

I keep it simple, and I only change the Model (mostly)
1. I just use "**Create new prompt**".

1. **Advanced Settings:** I don't open this.  Though Top P, if the model allows it, shows just the most probable words to "come next".  Not all models allow its use.
1. It saves your AI Query to Google AI Studios in Google Drive.
1. You can move the AI Query from the default location to another folder easy enough.
1. If you want to share the query with source material, I recommend sharing the drive folder, and move your query and reference materials into the same folder.

# **How I Created a Classroom Seating Chart Free with ChatGPT (Instructions)**

Hi teachers. I wanted to share a method I used to create a seating chart for my classroom using ChatGPT. It was easy and efficient. 

Here’s how I did it:
## 1. PREPARE YOUR STUDENT LIST

First, I prepared a list of my students' names in a simple text file. For privacy, I used first names only. Here’s an example of what my list looked like:

Alice, Bob, Charlie, Dana, Eve, Frank, Grace, Hank, Ivy, Jack, Luna, Mason, Nina, Oscar, Paul, Quincy, Rachel, Sam, Tina, Uma
## 2. DESCRIBE YOUR CLASSROOM LAYOUT

Next, I provided ChatGPT with details about my classroom setup, such as the number of rows and columns, and any special seating requirements. This is what my description included:

Classroom Layout:
* Rows: 5
* Columns: 4

Special Seating Requirements:
1. Alice needs to sit near the front due to vision issues.
1. Bob and Charlie work well together, place them in the same row.
1. Dana needs a quiet corner due to concentration difficulties.
1. Eve and Frank should not be seated next to each other.
1. Grace requires a seat close to the door for easy access.
1. Hank prefers to sit in the back.
## 3. INPUT STUDENT PREFERENCES

I made sure to include any specific seating preferences, like group work or special needs, to ensure the seating arrangement catered to everyone’s needs.
## 4. GENERATE THE SEATING CHART

I then asked ChatGPT to create a seating chart based on the provided information and the student names. My request looked something like this:

**Example Prompt:**

"ChatGPT, please arrange my students in a 5x4 seating chart considering the following preferences:

Classroom Layout: Rows: 5, Columns: 4

Special Seating Requirements:
1. Alice needs to sit near the front due to vision issues.
1. Bob and Charlie work well together, place them in the same row.
1. Dana needs a quiet corner due to concentration difficulties.
1. Eve and Frank should not be seated next to each other.
1. Grace requires a seat close to the door for easy access.
1. Hank prefers to sit in the back." + the attached file.
## 5. REVIEW AND ADJUST

After receiving the seating chart from ChatGPT, I reviewed it to ensure it fit my needs. I also had the option to export the final seating chart as a PDF or Excel document for easy access and sharing.
## 6. CUSTOM GPT FOR DOCUMENT UPLOADS

If you’re looking to automate this even further, you can create a custom GPT in ChatGPT (or Claude) with specific instructions on what to do with an uploaded document.
## FINAL THOUGHTS

Methods like this have saved me so much time and hassle, and I hope it helps you too!

If you need help with anything else, feel free to post it to the group. :)  Good luck! - Diana

# **Interactive AI Ideas to Energize Your Classroom**

Engaging students through interactive methods can make learning more dynamic and enjoyable. Here are some AI-driven interactive ideas to incorporate into your classroom:

**1. AI-Powered Quizzes and Games:** Create interactive quizzes and games that adapt to student performance, providing real-time feedback and varying the difficulty to keep students challenged and engaged.

**2. Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) Experiences:** Use AI-enhanced VR and AR tools to create immersive learning experiences. Students can explore historical sites, conduct virtual science experiments, or interact with 3D models to deepen their understanding of complex subjects.

**3. Interactive Storytelling:** Incorporate AI-driven storytelling apps that allow students to create and navigate through interactive stories, enhancing their creativity, comprehension, and engagement with the subject matter.

**5. Collaborative AI Projects:** Organize group projects where students use AI tools to solve real-world problems. Whether it’s building a simple AI model or using AI to analyze data, these projects promote teamwork and practical application of knowledge.

# **How to Spot AI-Plagiarized Essays (2024 Guide)**

AI-generated essays are becoming more common, and it's important to know how to identify them. Here are key signs that an essay might be plagiarized using AI:
## 1. **OVERLY PERFECT GRAMMAR**

AI tools often produce text with flawless grammar and punctuation. While this might seem like a positive, it's worth noting if the student's usual work doesn't reflect the same level of accuracy.
## 2. **UNIFORM WRITING STYLE**

AI-generated content typically maintains a consistent tone and style throughout. If an essay lacks the natural variations and personal touches of human writing, it might be AI-generated.
## 3. **REPETITIVE PHRASING**

AI models sometimes use repetitive phrases or synonyms in a way that feels unnatural. Look for repeated words or expressions that don't fit well with the overall context.
## 4. **LACK OF PERSONAL INSIGHT**

Essays that rely heavily on facts and general knowledge but lack personal anecdotes, opinions, or unique perspectives might be AI-written. AI tools struggle to produce content with genuine personal insight.
## 5. **UNUSUAL VOCABULARY**

AI-generated essays might use advanced vocabulary that seems out of place for the student's level. Sudden jumps in language complexity can be a red flag.
## 6. **INCONSISTENT QUALITY**

AI tools sometimes produce uneven content quality. A well-written section might be followed by a poorly constructed one, indicating that different parts were generated separately and then combined.
## 7. **ABSENCE OF CITATIONS**

AI-generated content might lack proper citations or reference styles. Check for inconsistencies in how sources are cited, or the complete absence of citations where they would typically be expected.
## 8. **GENERIC CONTENT**

AI essays often provide generic answers without diving deep into specifics. If an essay covers topics in a broad, superficial manner without detailed analysis, it might be AI-generated.

Leverage Prompt Templates for Efficient AI Interaction: A Guide for Teachers

When using AI in your teaching, starting with pre-built prompt templates for common tasks can save time and ensure consistency. By using and customizing these templates, you can streamline your workflow and improve the quality of AI-generated content for your classroom needs.

WHY USE PROMPT TEMPLATES

Think of prompt templates as a set of proven guidelines. Just as you wouldn’t start every lesson plan from scratch, using templates provides a solid foundation that you can adapt to your specific needs. This approach enhances efficiency and consistency in your teaching materials.

HOW TO LEVERAGE PROMPT TEMPLATES

Instead of creating a prompt from scratch: "Create a quiz about Chapter 5 of our textbook."

Start with a template: "Create a [content type] for [subject/topic]. Include [key details], focusing on [specific aspect]. Use a [tone and style]."

Customize it: "Create a quiz for Chapter 5 of our history textbook. Include multiple-choice questions, short answers, and one essay question. Focus on key events and their significance. Use a clear and student-friendly tone."

BENEFITS OF USING PROMPT TEMPLATES

1. Efficiency: Save time by starting with a well-structured template.

2. Consistency: Ensure all prompts follow a similar structure, leading to more predictable and reliable AI responses.

3. Flexibility: Easily adapt templates to fit different tasks and requirements.

TIPS FOR USING PROMPT TEMPLATES

1. Identify Common Tasks: Determine which tasks you frequently need AI assistance with and create templates for them.

2. Customize as Needed: Adjust templates to include specific details and requirements for each new task.

3. Refine Over Time: Continuously improve your templates based on the quality of AI responses you receive.

**The Mediocrity Machine**

During a recent creative writing lesson with a key stage 3 class I noticed several students using AI to assist in their work. I had previously discussed with the class the ways in which AI can and cannot be useful, but to facilitate a more controlled use of AI in the work I supplied them with a GDPR compliant chatbot that I created, using the Mizou platform, to ensure standardised guardrails and to offer limited help within clearly defined parameters. I allowed the student to get assistance with synonyms and examples of imagery and even to ask for feedback from the AI on short samples of their own writing.  Ultimately, the assessment was to be handwritten in their books, and they were allowed to use AI in the preparation stage, as long as they adhered to the clear guidelines I provided.

However, some students still attempted to generate large pieces of work using AI, overestimating its effectiveness and underestimating the importance of the learning process.

**The Experiment**

To demonstrate the limitations of AI in creative writing, I conducted an experiment in a following lesson. I created a detailed prompt for describing a desert scene and fed it into four different AI models. Despite producing seemingly different descriptions, closer examination revealed striking similarities in structure, style, and the use of clichés.

**Student Observations**

I presented the AI-generated descriptions to the students on a single worksheet. Initially impressed, the students soon discovered the similarities between the texts when they looked beyond the micro-focus on impressive vocabulary and imagery. They identified patterns in personification, sensory language, and the use of poetic and metaphorical language.

**Why so average?**

The ‘sameyness’ of the AI generated texts can be explained when we consider the mechanism behind the ‘Artificial Intelligence’ (oh how I wish this term had never come into use…).

Given that what the AI is doing is aggregating all of the examples of descriptions of deserts that it can get and then blending them to reach a sort of ‘average’ it is hardly surprising that what happened was an underlying level of similarity.

What was stark was that the students could see it and so could I.

The classroom takeaway - hopefully my students will now see how much more creative and interesting they are than an AI.

**Implications**

This experiment highlighted the importance of teaching students the strengths and limitations of AI in the writing process. While AI can be useful for providing alternatives, serving as a thesaurus, and offering feedback on the effectiveness of one's work, it falls short in terms of creativity and originality. As educators, we must focus on developing students' own creative abilities and building their confidence before introducing AI as an enhancement tool.

Read more details on my blog:

[https://theaienglishteacher.wordpress.com/2024/06/12/the-mediocrity-machine/](https://theaienglishteacher.wordpress.com/2024/06/12/the-mediocrity-machine/)

Microsoft announced a number of AI enhancements for Teams this month, putting generative AI directly into its main Educational Platform - is this the way of the future?

**Clippy has arrived to help you set assignments!**

So I was setting a couple of assignments for my classes today and what should I discover in Teams? An AI enhancement that I’d never seen before!

In the assignment there appeared several options to add enhancements directly through generative AI, such as assessment criteria, enumerated steps and key work highlighting.

**The additional features are:**

📚 **AI Assignment Instructions Generation**: Educators can use AI to create detailed assignment instructions tailored to grade level and language preferences.

📊 **AI Generated Rubrics**: A new feature that allows educators to generate rubrics using AI, with options to customise and evaluate student work effectively.

🔍 **Reading Progress Passage Generation**: AI technology helps create personalised reading passages for students, with adjustable complexity and the ability to include challenging words.

❓ **Comprehension Questions with AI**: AI assists in generating a set of comprehension questions for reading passages, which can be customised and edited by educators.

Now the instruction and rubric generation tools are… well, they’re okay at best. The main issue, as is often the case, is that you can either regenerate or edit the output, but there is no way to iterate the content as you are at remove away from the LLM being employed. The practice rubric I created was fine, but I’ve had better and more nuanced results working with Anthropic’s latest version of Claude AI. Yes, I may use a paid premium version, but even the free version is more intuitive and, more importantly, it has the ability to iterate outputs and respond conversationally to the user.

Where the system seems to have more application is in the reading progress generator and comprehension questions. Now like the rubrics these are a one shot deal, but they are tied to the Microsoft Reading Coach system and are used to create and track reading fluency. The fact that these systems are integrated and the data analysis of student performance comes straight into the LMS is really powerful and it is here that this use case gets really interesting.

What is happening here may not be a huge leap forward in terms of AI capability, but what it represents is the integration of AI directly into pre-existing platforms.

The question is whether this is the future direction of travel and, if so, whether it will prove useful?

I guess time will tell.
